climate.overview_html: The pre-COP31 picture sharpened on 22 October when the European Parliament voted to adopt its negotiating mandate for Antalya — calling for a faster fossil fuel phase-out, a fossil fuel non-proliferation treaty, and greater climate finance for vulnerable nations. The mandate was adopted 50–16 in committee and sets up a direct confrontation with China and Saudi Arabia over both the pace of fossil fuel phase-out and the CBAM’s legality. The backdrop remains the UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2026, which declared the 1.5°C no-or-limited-overshoot pathway lost and current policies tracking to 2.6–2.8°C, and the early COP31 speakers list showing only 77 world leaders registered — down a third from COP28’s 116. With the conference opening in 15 days, the convergence of low leader attendance, the UNEP emissions trajectory, and a European Parliament calling for a treaty most G20 members will oppose signals a diplomatically difficult Antalya.

items.source: Carbon Pulse / Brussels Times / EU Parliament
items.headline: European Parliament Adopts COP31 Negotiating Mandate: Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty, Faster Phase-Out, Greater Climate Finance for Vulnerable Nations; 50–16 Committee Vote
items.summary: The European Parliament adopted its formal negotiating position for COP31 on October 22, calling for the EU to take a leading role toward a fossil fuel non-proliferation treaty, a clear and specific timetable to phase out fossil fuel production, and an end to fossil fuel subsidies. The mandate also calls for climate finance that does not worsen developing countries' debt burdens and opposes double-counting of existing funds toward the new collective quantified goal. A European Parliament delegation led by MEP Lídia Pereira will be on-site at Antalya from November 16–20. The mandate's fossil fuel non-proliferation treaty position sets up a direct clash with Saudi Arabia, India and China at COP31.

items.headline: Only 77 Leaders Registered to Speak at COP31 World Leaders’ Summit — Down a Third from COP28’s 116; France, Germany, Italy, India, Canada, Japan Absent; Former UN Climate Chief Calls Low Turnout a “Poor Signal”
items.summary: An early provisional UN speakers' list shows only 77 heads of state or government registered to address the COP31 World Leaders' Summit in Antalya on November 11–12 — down from 116 at COP28 in Dubai and 144 at COP27 in Sharm el-Sheikh. Notable absentees include the leaders of France, Germany, Italy, India, Russia, Canada and Japan. China is expected to be represented by Vice-Premier Ding Xuexiang rather than President Xi Jinping. Former UN climate secretariat chief Yvo de Boer said 'climate action needs a strong show of support, not empty seats at a leaders' summit'.

items.headline: UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2026 “The Point of Return”: 1.5°C Overshoot Now Inevitable; Global Emissions Flat at 58.4 GtCO<sub>2</sub>e in 2025; Current Policies Track to 2.6–2.8°C; US Leads G20 Emissions Rise
items.summary: UNEP's annual Emissions Gap Report, released October 21 and titled 'The Point of Return', officially declares that the opportunity to limit warming to 1.5°C with 'no or limited' overshoot has been lost. Global GHG emissions were approximately 58.4 GtCO₂e in 2025 — essentially unchanged from 2024. A lowest-possible-overshoot path requires cuts of 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035, and 69% by 2040, plus removal of approximately 320 Gt CO₂. Among G20 nations, the US logged the largest emissions increase (+133 Mt CO₂e). Solar PV capacity has grown seven times faster than projected since Paris.

items.headline: COP31 Names 10 Co-Facilitators: Bowen Appoints Five Ministerial Pairs Covering Finance, Adaptation, Mitigation, Just Transition and Oceans; Turkey Expects 85 World Leaders, Record 159 Pavilions
items.summary: Australian Climate Change Minister Chris Bowen announced ten co-facilitators — five ministerial pairs — covering the key negotiating tracks at Antalya: climate finance, adaptation, mitigation, just transition, and oceans. Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum said Turkey expects 85 world leaders at the World Leaders' Summit, with a record 159 pavilions. Turkey is framing COP31 as a 'policies implementation' summit focused on operationalising the Baku Finance Goal, Loss and Damage Fund, and Article 6 carbon markets.

items.headline: China Sets COP31 Priorities: Demands Detailed Roadmap for US$300 Billion Annual Climate Finance Goal, Opposes Carbon Border Mechanisms, Pledges to Speak for Developing Nations
items.summary: China's Vice Minister of Ecology and Environment Li Gao published Beijing's COP31 positions on October 21–22: (1) a concrete implementation roadmap for the US$300 billion annual climate finance goal; (2) opposing the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism as a violation of UNFCCC common-but-differentiated responsibilities; (3) demanding the global stocktake focus on developed-nation implementation gaps; (4) tripling adaptation finance.

items.headline: UN Secretary-General Guterres: World Falling “Dangerously Short” on Climate Action; El Niño and Record Heat Amplify Urgency Ahead of COP31
items.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres called the world 'dangerously short' on climate action, referencing record-breaking heat, devastating floods, and an unprecedented El Niño as making accelerated action 'ever more urgent'. With COP31 in Antalya opening November 9, diplomatic pressure is intensifying.

items.headline: South Africa at COP31: Pushes for Substantially More Adaptation Finance; Aligns with G77 Demand to Triple Adaptation Funding by 2035
items.summary: South Africa is entering COP31 with adaptation finance as its top priority, arguing developing nations most vulnerable to climate shocks have been shortchanged in NCQG negotiations. South Africa aligns with G77 demands for adaptation finance to be tripled by 2035.

major_events.name: Typhoon Champi (Rosal, No. 30) — Taiwan Power Outages 25 Oct; Okinawa 567 mm Rainfall Record; Kyushu Approach ~Mon 26 Oct; Extratropical Transition Tue 27 Oct
major_events.status: As of 25 Oct: Champi passed Taiwan’s northeast coast, cutting off power to parts of Taiwan before continuing north. Current intensity (~0900 UTC 25 Oct): centre near 28.3°N 123.8°E, moving NNE at 21 kph; sustained winds 97 kph / gusts 121 kph. Iriomote Island (Okinawa) recorded 567 mm over 48 hours — a new local record; Owase, Mie received 329 mm in 24 hours. JMA continues to forecast a Kyushu approach ~Monday 26 October followed by extratropical transition south of Honshu by Tuesday 27 October. JTWC rates both track and intensity confidence as low; residual risk of the subtropical high pushing the storm westward toward the Taiwan Strait remains.
major_events.impact: Taiwan: power outages northeastern coast; island-wide shutdown (schools, stock exchange, 600+ flights) lifted 24 Oct; post-passage assessment ongoing. Japan: JMA heavy rain advisories for northern Kyushu, Chugoku, Kinki, Hokuriku; land warnings expected as system approaches. Okinawa: 567 mm 48-hour record at Iriomote. Mie: 329 mm 24-hour total at Owase. Korea: rain and wind expected in southern regions through the weekend.

major_events.name: Invest 98B / Potential Cyclone Arnab — Bay of Bengal; IMD Forecasts Cyclonic Storm by 26 Oct; Andhra Pradesh Coast Approach ~28 Oct
major_events.status: As of 24–25 Oct: India’s IMD Special Message No. 3 projects that Invest 98B will intensify into a deep depression by 25 October and a cyclonic storm by the morning of 26 October, then approach the Andhra Pradesh coast around 28 October. Current: central pressure ~1004 hPa, winds ~50 kph; very warm SSTs with moderate 15–20 knot wind shear. Skymet warns North Coastal AP and South Coastal Odisha are most susceptible to a direct hit. JTWC meteorologist Andy Hazelton noted conditions are “favorable for organization and intensification” and the system “could be a very strong TC.” Some media are calling it “Cyclone Arnab” though official IMD naming is pending.
major_events.impact: Andhra Pradesh: most susceptible coastline; evacuation alerts expected as system intensifies. Odisha, West Bengal, Jharkhand, Bihar: heavy rain and wind alerts. Tamil Nadu, Karnataka: heavy rain alerts. IMD issuing updated bulletins every 6 hours.

major_events.name: SE Asian Peatland Haze (Indonesia/Borneo/Sumatra) — Worst in >10 Years; 1,104 Hotspots; 1,700+ Estimated Deaths; Foreign Assistance Now Approved; ASMC Level 3 Alert Continues
major_events.status: As of 24–25 Oct: Reuters characterises Indonesia’s 2026 fires as the worst in more than a decade. Indonesia’s environment ministry logged 1,104 hotspots — approximately four times the count from the previous Monday — with Central Kalimantan showing the sharpest rise. An estimated 1,700+ deaths from fire-related haze pollution have been recorded. After initial resistance, Foreign Minister Nasir confirmed on 16 October that President Prabowo has approved foreign assistance from neighbouring countries; 162 arrests have been made for allegedly starting illegal fires. Gradual monsoon onset expected late October/November. ASMC Level 3 alert in force for Southern ASEAN.
major_events.impact: Indonesia: 283,270+ respiratory illness cases (7 provinces); 162 arrests for fire-starting; protests over national disaster declaration. Malaysia: school closures; parliament debating air purifier tax rebates. Singapore: Transboundary Haze Pollution Act enforcement active. Timor-Leste: schools closed. ~40 million people exposed across Kalimantan and Sumatra. Super El Niño + positive IOD continue to suppress monsoon rainfall.

weather.overview_html: Three concurrent high-impact events on 25 October. Typhoon Champi passed Taiwan’s northeast coast, knocking out power to parts of the island and producing a 567 mm 48-hour rainfall record on Iriomote Island (Okinawa), before its forecast Kyushu approach on Monday 26 October and extratropical transition Tuesday. A second, potentially more acute threat has emerged in the Bay of Bengal: IMD is forecasting Invest 98B to become a cyclonic storm by 26 October and approach the Andhra Pradesh coast around 28 October, with JTWC flagging potential for “very strong TC” intensity. Meanwhile, Indonesia’s peatland fire crisis — now the worst in more than a decade per Reuters — has seen hotspot counts quadruple week-on-week to 1,104, with Indonesia finally approving foreign assistance after initial resistance.

items.headline: Typhoon Champi 25 Oct: Cuts Power in Northeastern Taiwan; Okinawa 567 mm 48-Hour Record; 97 kph Sustained Approaching Kyushu ~26 Oct; Extratropical Transition 27 Oct
items.summary: On October 25, Typhoon Champi made its closest pass to Taiwan's northeast coast, cutting off power to parts of the island before continuing northward. Weather Underground placed the centre at approximately 28.3°N, 123.8°E, moving NNE at 21 kph, with maximum sustained winds of 97 kph and gusts of 121 kph. Iriomote Island in Okinawa recorded 567 mm of rain over 48 hours — a new local record; Owase in Mie Prefecture received 329 mm in 24 hours. JMA continues to forecast a closest approach to Kyushu around Monday October 26, followed by extratropical transition south of Honshu by October 27. Heavy rain advisories remain in force for northern Kyushu, Chugoku, Kinki, and Hokuriku. JTWC rates both track and intensity confidence as low. Taiwan's island-wide shutdown was lifted on October 24 after the storm passed without a direct landfall.

items.headline: IMD Forecasts Cyclonic Storm in Bay of Bengal by 26 Oct; Invest 98B to Approach Andhra Pradesh Coast ~28 Oct; North Coastal AP and South Coastal Odisha Most at Risk; JTWC Notes “Very Strong TC” Potential
items.summary: India's Meteorological Department issued Special Message No. 3 on October 24, projecting Invest 98B will intensify into a deep depression by October 25 and a cyclonic storm by the morning of October 26, then approach the Andhra Pradesh coast around October 28. Central pressure ~1004 hPa; sustained winds ~50 kph; very warm sea surface temperatures with moderate 15–20 knot wind shear. Skymet warned that North Coastal Andhra Pradesh and South Coastal Odisha face the highest risk of a direct hit, with Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, West Bengal, Jharkhand and Bihar all under heavy rain and wind alerts. JTWC meteorologist Andy Hazelton described conditions as 'favorable for organization and intensification' and noted the system 'could be a very strong TC'. Several media outlets are referring to the system as 'Cyclone Arnab' — which would be India's first named cyclone of 2026 — though official IMD naming was pending as of October 25.

items.source: France 24 / The Vibes / The Rakyat Post / Wikipedia
items.headline: Indonesia Peatland Haze Day 30+: Worst in >10 Years; 1,104 Hotspots (4× Prior Week); 1,700+ Estimated Deaths; Indonesia Approves Foreign Assistance; 162 Arrests; Monsoon Onset Still Weeks Away
items.summary: Reuters described Indonesia's 2026 peatland fire crisis as the country's worst forest fires in more than a decade. Indonesia's environment ministry logged 1,104 hotspots — approximately four times the count from the previous Monday — with Central Kalimantan recording the sharpest increase. An estimated 1,700+ deaths from fire-related haze pollution have been recorded, with 283,270+ respiratory illness cases across seven provinces. After initial resistance, Foreign Minister Arrmanatha Nasir confirmed on October 16 that President Prabowo had approved acceptance of foreign assistance from neighbouring countries; 162 people have been arrested for allegedly starting illegal fires. The haze has spread to Malaysia (school closures), Singapore (Transboundary Haze Pollution Act enforcement), and Timor-Leste (school closures). Forecasters expect gradual monsoon onset across Sumatra and Kalimantan in late October and November. A Super El Niño and positive Indian Ocean Dipole continue to suppress rainfall. ASMC Level 3 alert remains in force.

renewables.overview_html: Two new transactions this week extend the trend of institutional capital consolidating operational renewable assets. Greencoat UK Wind acquired the remaining 20% of a 96.4 MW five-site UK wind portfolio from EDF Invest on 15 October, taking full ownership and entering a joint repowering arrangement with EDF Power Solutions. On 9 October, Integrated Power Services (IPS) acquired Bold Renewables, the exclusive OEM service provider for over 4 GW of Advanced Energy central solar inverters across 3,000+ US and Canadian sites. Both deals sit alongside the week’s larger-scale items: the Applied Digital / Soluna AI data-centre colocation on Texas wind (50 MW compute co-located with 150 MW Briscoe Wind Farm), China Huaneng’s 960 MW wind-solar-storage hybrid full grid connection in Inner Mongolia, and EirGrid’s data showing 15% of Irish wind electricity wasted in H1 2026 due to grid infrastructure lag.

items.headline: Integrated Power Services Acquires Bold Renewables: OEM Service Provider for >4 GW of Advanced Energy Central Solar Inverters Across 3,000+ US/Canadian Sites; Full-Lifecycle Solar Service Platform
items.summary: Integrated Power Services (IPS), backed by Searchlight Capital, acquired Bold Renewables (Windsor, Colorado) effective October 9, 2026. Bold is the exclusive OEM source of field service, spare parts, and preventive maintenance for Advanced Energy central solar inverters under the Solaron, NX, TX, and PV Powered brands — covering approximately 14,000 legacy inverters, over 4 GW of capacity, across more than 3,000 sites in the US and Canada. Bold joins IPS's Motion division alongside ENA Electronics, extending IPS's coverage across wind, solar, mining, and industrial inverter service markets. Terms were not disclosed.

items.headline: Greencoat UK Wind Acquires Remaining 20% of 96.4 MW Five-Site UK Wind Portfolio from EDF Invest; Takes Full Ownership; Enters Joint Repowering Development Arrangement with EDF Power Solutions
items.summary: Greencoat UK Wind acquired a 20% stake in a 96.4 MW portfolio of five wind farms in the UK from EDF Invest, taking its total ownership to 100%. Consolidating ownership gives Greencoat full operational control; it simultaneously entered a joint development arrangement with EDF Power Solutions to progress repowering of the sites. Existing operations and maintenance arrangements with EDF remain in place. Terms were not disclosed.

items.headline: Applied Digital and Soluna Holdings Sign Definitive Agreement for 50 MW AI Data Centre at Briscoe County, Texas, Co-Located with 150 MW Briscoe Wind Farm; Wind + Grid Hybrid Power for AI Compute
items.summary: Applied Digital Corporation and Soluna Holdings signed a definitive agreement to jointly develop a 50 MW AI data centre in Briscoe County, Texas. The facility will be co-located adjacent to the 150 MW Briscoe Wind Farm and draw power from a combination of wind generation and grid electricity, designed to absorb curtailment periods while providing firm compute capacity for AI workloads.

items.headline: China Huaneng Fully Grid-Connects 960 MW Wind-Solar-Storage Hybrid in Inner Mongolia: 810 MW Wind + 150 MW Solar + 60 MW/240 MWh Grid-Forming BESS; First Integrated Coal-Renewables Retrofit of This Scale in China
items.summary: China Huaneng announced the full grid connection of a 960 MW wind-solar-storage project at Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia, comprising 810 MW wind, 150 MW solar PV, a 60 MW/240 MWh grid-forming BESS, and a 20 Mvar STATCOM, paired with a coal-fired plant in flexible dispatch mode. Described as the first project of this kind in China; expected annual output approximately 2.3 billion kWh.

items.headline: EirGrid Data: 15% of Ireland’s Wind Electricity Wasted H1 2026 Due to Grid Constraints; Enough to Power 667,000 Homes; 13%+ of All Renewables Curtailed First Nine Months
items.summary: EirGrid figures reveal that more than 13% of available wind and solar electricity in Ireland during the first nine months of 2026 could not be used due to grid constraints. In H1 alone, 15% of wind electricity was dispatched down — enough to power approximately 667,000 Irish homes — worsening from 2025 curtailment rates. Experts cite a multi-year lag between accelerating renewable capacity additions and major transmission infrastructure investment.

items.headline: AMEA Power Signs 250 MW/1,000 MWh Battery Storage Project Agreements for Uzbekistan’s Bukhara Region; Central Asia’s Largest Battery Commitment of 2026
items.summary: UAE-based AMEA Power signed project agreements on October 16 for a 250 MW / 1,000 MWh BESS in Uzbekistan's Bukhara region. This adds to AMEA Power's existing 150 MW / 300 MWh BESS under construction near Tashkent, bringing total committed Uzbekistan storage to 400 MW / 1,300 MWh. No deal price disclosed.

items.headline: Atmos Renewables Acquires BayWa r.e.’s Australian Renewable Portfolio — Yatpool Solar (106 MW), Hughenden Solar (20 MW), Bullawah Wind Development (~800 MW) — Total Capacity Exceeds 2 GW
items.summary: Atmos Renewables (Igneo Infrastructure Partners) finalised on October 16 the acquisition of BayWa r.e.'s Australian portfolio: Yatpool Solar Park (106 MW, Victoria), Hughenden Solar Park (20 MW, Queensland), and the Bullawah Wind Farm development (~800 MW wind + 359 MW/718 MWh BESS). The deal pushes Atmos's combined operating and in-construction capacity beyond 2 GW. BayWa r.e. is retreating from non-core markets amid its parent company's financial restructuring. Baker McKenzie advised BayWa; no price disclosed.

items.headline: Foresight Energy Infrastructure Partners II Acquires Nivala BESS — Finland’s Largest Battery Storage System — from Fotowatio Renewable Ventures; Nordic Grid-Balancing Assets Attract Growing Institutional Capital
items.summary: Foresight Energy Infrastructure Partners II completed its acquisition of 100% of Nivala BESS — Finland's largest battery energy storage system — from Fotowatio Renewable Ventures (FRV), the renewables subsidiary of Abdul Latif Jameel. Nivala provides frequency and voltage regulation services in Finland's electricity market. No deal price disclosed.

science.overview_html: Two new papers this week sharpen the picture on AI weather model performance at the extremes. arXiv:2610.20519 (Wessel et al., 14 Oct) reverses the headline of earlier benchmarking work: on a like-for-like probabilistic basis, probabilistic AI models outperform ECMWF IFS-ENS on record-breaking heat events, with WeatherNext2 sitting 24% above IFS-ENS on Brier skill score at 72-hour lead time — directly updating the earlier Carbon Brief-covered finding that physics-based models outperform AI on extremes (which had used deterministic models). The complementary review by Beucler, Neelin et al. (arXiv:2610.09770) maps the theoretical gap between current AI weather skill and the climate-scale forced responses needed for decarbonisation planning. Both papers land against the backdrop of active Champi and Bay of Bengal events where the arXiv:2610.22077 finding of strong AI track skill but weak intensity and ensemble spread remains operationally relevant.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.20519 — Probabilistic AI Models Outperform NWP on Record-Breaking Heat Extremes: WeatherNext2 24% above IFS-ENS Brier Skill Score at 72 h; Reverses Earlier Deterministic Benchmarking Verdict
items.meta: Wessel, Spuler, Ferro, Kretschmer, Sippel · arXiv:2610.20519 · 14 Oct 2026
items.summary: Jakob Benjamin Wessel, Fiona Spuler, Christopher Ferro, Marlene Kretschmer and Sebastian Sippel test probabilistic AI weather models against ECMWF IFS-ENS on record-breaking heat events over global land in 2022. Key finding: on a like-for-like probabilistic basis, WeatherNext2's Brier skill score sits 24% above IFS-ENS at 72-hour lead time. The authors argue that earlier work comparing deterministic AI outputs against deterministic NWP was an unfair comparison. This directly reverses the headline conclusion from a 2026 Science Advances study (covered by Carbon Brief and Physics World) that found physics-based HRES outperforming deterministic AI models on 2020 record-breaking events — the key difference being deterministic vs. probabilistic model generation. The finding is based on 2022 global land data and is subject to choice of scoring rule.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.09770 — “Artificial Intelligence Pathways from Weather to Climate” (Beucler, Neelin et al.): AI Weather Skill Does Not Transfer to Climate Projections Without Explicit Forcing Representation and Out-of-Distribution Stress-Testing
items.meta: Beucler (UNIL), Neelin (UCLA) + 10 co-authors incl. Bretherton, Watt-Meyer, Schneider, Zanna · arXiv:2610.09770 · 7 Oct 2026
items.summary: Tom Beucler (University of Lausanne), David Neelin (UCLA) and ten co-authors review the state of AI weather models and the gap between weather-scale skill and climate-scale projection fidelity. Main arguments: (1) AI models achieve well-calibrated ensemble weather forecasts but do not produce credible forced responses to external climate drivers such as greenhouse gases or land-use change without explicit representation of those forcings; (2) out-of-distribution robustness testing on extremes and counterfactual scenarios is required before models can inform adaptation decisions; (3) AI models are not intrinsically more computationally efficient than GPU-ported dynamical models once complexity is accounted for; (4) ML downscaling can partly substitute for fine-scale resolution where observations are available. Presented at IPAM (UCLA) and KIT seminars.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.22555 — AI Foundation Model for Atmospheric Chemistry and Climate: R<sup>2</sup> > 0.85 on 23/27 Fields; ~100× Faster than UKCA; Enables Tractable High-Resolution Chemistry-Climate Simulation
items.summary: This paper fine-tunes the Aurora Earth system model on atmospheric chemistry and climate simulations from UKCA, producing an AI foundation model that predicts 27 atmospheric chemistry and climate fields; 23 of 27 achieve R² above 0.85. The model runs approximately 100 times faster than the physics-based UKCA model and remains stable in autoregressive simulation over 50 years. An emulator at this accuracy threshold opens the door to routine inclusion in AI-driven climate projection pipelines.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.26145 — Hourly Precipitation Downscaling from km-Scale Regional Climate Simulations; NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Tackling Climate Change with Machine Learning
items.meta: Addison, Kendon, Watson · arXiv:2610.26145 [physics.ao-ph] · 20 Oct 2026 · NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Tackling Climate Change with ML
items.summary: Henry Addison, Elizabeth Kendon and Peter Watson present a deep-learning approach to downscaling hourly precipitation from kilometre-scale regional climate model simulations to sub-kilometre scales relevant to impact applications (urban flooding, hydrology, agriculture). Addresses a key bottleneck: as convection-permitting km-scale RCMs become feasible for multi-decade climate runs, translating their output to sub-km scales for adaptation planning remains computationally prohibitive without statistical downscaling.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.22077 — Evaluating Probabilistic AI Weather Models on Tropical Cyclones: Strong Track Skill; Intensity and Ensemble Spread Remain Weak Points vs. ECMWF IFS-ENS
items.summary: This paper benchmarks leading probabilistic AI weather models on tropical cyclone forecasting. Key findings: AI models outperform ECMWF IFS-ENS at cyclone track forecasting across multiple lead times. However, intensity forecasting and ensemble spread calibration remain weak — models underweight rare, high-intensity values via training objectives that favour large-scale atmospheric state skill. The failure modes — strong track skill, weak intensity and spread — are directly observable in the ongoing Typhoon Champi and Invest 98B (Bay of Bengal) forecast uncertainty.

items.headline: Mouatadid et al. in Nature: Probabilistic Bias Correction Doubles AI Subseasonal Forecast Skill at 2–6 Weeks; Improves ECMWF IFS for 92% of Temperature and 98% of Precipitation Targets; Leads SubX Competition
items.summary: Published in Nature, this paper introduces probabilistic bias correction (PBC) as a post-processing method for AI subseasonal forecasts in the 2–6-week range. PBC doubles AI subseasonal forecast skill relative to the uncorrected AI baseline; improves ECMWF's dynamical IFS for 92% of temperature prediction targets and 98% of precipitation targets globally; and leads the SubX international subseasonal forecast competition. Implies existing AI weather models have substantial latent skill at subseasonal timescales masked by poorly calibrated probability distributions — significant for operational S2S forecasting and renewable energy planning applications.

items.headline: DWD AICON-Global: One Year of Operational Verification Complete; Competitive with ICON NWP for Surface Variables at Short-to-Medium Range; Data Publicly Available Since March 2026
items.meta: arXiv:2608.24651 · DWD / Germany · data available since March 2026
items.summary: DWD's AICON-Global — Germany's operational AI-based deterministic global weather forecasting model — has completed approximately one year of operational verification since data became publicly available in March 2026. The model runs on the same horizontal grid as ICON-Global (~13 km), uses the Anemoi graph neural network framework, and is initialised every three hours. Verification shows AICON performs competitively with the operational ICON NWP system for surface variables in the short to medium range. Spectral analysis confirms damping of mesoscale activity relative to physics-based ICON; precipitation skill is comparable with noted limitations.

items.title: Hy24 Signs Agreement to Acquire Hynamics — EDF’s Low-Carbon Hydrogen Subsidiary — Through Its €2 Billion Clean Hydrogen Infrastructure Fund; 9 Projects in France and UK Including 120 MW Fawley Green Hydrogen; Closing Expected Q1 2027
items.body_html: Hy24 — a joint venture between Ardian and FiveT Hydrogen managing the world’s largest dedicated hydrogen investment platform at €2 billion — signed an agreement on 14 October to acquire Hynamics from EDF Pulse Ventures. Hynamics, founded by EDF in 2019, currently operates nine projects across France and the UK, including the 120 MW Fawley Green Hydrogen project, targeting heavy mobility and industrial applications. EDF is refocusing on nuclear and core power generation; Hy24 will scale Hynamics through its Clean Hydrogen Infrastructure fund. Transaction closing expected Q1 2027, pending regulatory approvals. Deal price not disclosed.
items.source_html: ESG Today / EDF Press Release

items.title: Greencoat UK Wind Acquires Remaining 20% Stake in 96.4 MW Five-Site UK Wind Portfolio from EDF Invest; Takes Full Ownership; Enters Joint Repowering Arrangement with EDF Power Solutions
items.body_html: Greencoat UK Wind acquired a 20% stake in a 96.4 MW five-wind-farm UK portfolio from EDF Invest, taking full ownership. Greencoat simultaneously entered a joint development arrangement with EDF Power Solutions to progress repowering of the sites; existing O&M arrangements with EDF remain in place. Financial terms not disclosed.

items.title: CarbonFarm Closes Oversubscribed €7 Million Series A Led by Colam Impact: AI-Satellite MRV Platform for Rice Decarbonisation, 19 Countries; Partners Include Diageo, Mars Food, BASF, World Bank
items.body_html: Paris-based CarbonFarm closed an oversubscribed €7 million Series A on 13 October, led by Colam Impact with participation from Proparco, Suma Capital, elea, Working Capital Fund, Albo and Bpifrance. CarbonFarm provides digital MRV for rice farming decarbonisation, combining AI-powered satellite imagery, field-data collection tools and GHG modelling to quantify methane emissions at field level. Rice cultivation accounts for approximately 12% of human-caused methane emissions globally; improved water management can cut emissions by up to 50% without affecting yields. The company now operates in 19 countries and counts Diageo, Mars Food, BASF Agricultural Solutions and the World Bank among its partners. Capital will fund expansion in Asia, Africa and Latin America.

items.title: Integrated Power Services Acquires Bold Renewables: OEM Service Provider for >4 GW of Advanced Energy Central Solar Inverters Across 3,000+ US/Canadian Sites; Full Solar+Wind Lifecycle Service Platform
items.body_html: Integrated Power Services (IPS), backed by Searchlight Capital, acquired Bold Renewables (Windsor, Colorado) effective 9 October, adding the exclusive OEM service and parts source for Advanced Energy central solar inverters under the Solaron, NX, TX and PV Powered brands. Bold supports approximately 14,000 legacy inverters covering over 4 GW of capacity across more than 3,000 solar sites in the US and Canada. Bold joins IPS’s Motion division alongside ENA Electronics, positioning IPS across wind, solar, mining, and industrial inverter service markets. Weil advised IPS and Searchlight Capital on debt financing for Bold and a concurrent add-on acquisition (Belyea Company). Terms not disclosed.

items.title: Applied Digital and Soluna Holdings Sign Definitive Agreement for 50 MW AI Data Centre Adjacent to 150 MW Briscoe Wind Farm, Texas; Wind + Grid Hybrid Power for AI Compute Colocation
items.body_html: Applied Digital Corporation and Soluna Holdings signed a definitive agreement on approximately 22 October to jointly develop a 50 MW AI data centre in Briscoe County, Texas, co-located with the 150 MW Briscoe Wind Farm. Power supply mixes wind generation with grid electricity to absorb curtailment while delivering firm AI compute capacity — part of a growing wave of AI infrastructure projects seeking renewable colocation to reduce grid interconnect costs and carbon intensity.

items.title: Atmos Renewables (Igneo Infrastructure Partners) Acquires BayWa r.e.’s Australian Renewable Portfolio — Yatpool Solar (106 MW), Hughenden Solar (20 MW), Bullawah Wind Development (~800 MW) — Total Capacity Exceeds 2 GW
items.body_html: Atmos Renewables finalised on 16 October the acquisition of BayWa r.e.’s Australian portfolio, adding operating solar parks at Yatpool (106 MW, Victoria) and Hughenden (20 MW, Queensland), plus the late-stage Bullawah Wind Farm development (~800 MW wind + 359 MW/718 MWh BESS). The deal pushes Atmos’s combined operating and in-construction capacity beyond 2 GW. BayWa r.e. is retreating from non-core markets amid its parent company’s financial restructuring. Baker McKenzie advised BayWa; no price disclosed.
items.source_html: PV Magazine Australia / Baker McKenzie

items.title: Foresight Energy Infrastructure Partners II Acquires Nivala BESS — Finland’s Largest Battery Storage System — from Fotowatio Renewable Ventures (Abdul Latif Jameel); Nordic Grid-Balancing Assets Attract Institutional Capital
items.body_html: Foresight Energy Infrastructure Partners II completed the acquisition of 100% of Nivala BESS — Finland’s largest battery energy storage system — from Fotowatio Renewable Ventures (FRV), the renewables subsidiary of Abdul Latif Jameel. Nivala provides frequency and voltage regulation services in Finland’s electricity market. No deal price disclosed. Continues a pattern of pan-European institutional funds acquiring operational Nordic BESS assets as ancillary services revenue models mature.

items.title: XCF Global Completes All-Stock Three-Way Merger Combining Renewable Fuel Production, Biomass-to-Fuels Development (Southern Energy Renewables) and Carbon-Asset Monetisation (DevvStream); Integrated Lifecycle Platform
items.body_html: XCF Global completed an all-stock three-way business combination on 19 October, merging renewable fuel production with Southern Energy Renewables’ biomass-to-fuels pipeline and DevvStream’s carbon-asset monetisation platform. The combined entity targets the full value chain of biomass-based fuel projects from production through carbon credit generation. No deal terms disclosed.
